chunk_findings.detail: After the named item is validated, it is re-resolved to its parent via `st.items.get(origin.port_of) or origin`, but the `removed` guard is not re-checked on the parent. The guard that *is* present (`if origin is None or origin.removed:`) only makes sense if removed items stay retrievable in `st.items`, so the lookup can return a removed fix. Concrete input: `FIX` exists with `removed=True` (still in `st.items`) and its port `FIX@2` is present (e.g. an orphaned/landed port, `port_of == "FIX"`, not removed). Running `task add FIX2 --port-of FIX@2` passes `origin is None or origin.removed` (it names the live port), then `origin` becomes the removed `FIX`, and `family`/`wanted` are built from the removed fix's lines. The follow-up silently succeeds and ports onto the lines of a removed fix instead of returning `--port-of: no such item`, which is exactly the failure the direct guard was meant to produce; the same bypass occurs for naming `FIX` itself if the fix remains in the dict marked removed but the guard were the only check.

chunk_findings.detail: `port_of` is registered on the wrong MCP tool's `properties` map. The properties block that contains the `lines` parameter (line ~681, followed by its own `readd`) belongs to the handler at line ~706 that forwards `port_of` to the add API — this is the fix tool that must expose the new property. The `"port_of"` entry was instead added above the `readd` entry at line ~601, inside the other tool's property map (the one whose preceding property is the single-line "…tasks inherit a phase's line" text, and which already has its own `readd` entry). Concrete failure: an MCP client that builds arguments from the schema of the `lines`-taking tool cannot send `port_of` at all (it is absent from that tool's `inputSchema`), and if the server validates against the schema it rejects `{"lines":"1,2,3","port_of":"FIX"}` as an unknown property; the `port_of` feature is reachable from the CLI but not from the MCP tool that supports `lines`, while the other tool now advertises a `port_of` property whose handler ignores it.
